description: Emphasizes an attack at an EXACT time you specify (mode 3 of 4; siblings: 1 = first level above a gate, 2 = max level within +-200 ms of an approximate time, 4 = the file's overall max): a gain envelope rises over onset ms to the attack point and decays back over decay ms, boosting just that moment. Boost locality verified: gain 1.5 at time 0.55 lifted only the 0.55-0.58 s region (10 ms window analysis), leaving the rest untouched; duration static and exact at both probed input durations. RUNTIME HEADROOM GATE: if the boosted attack would exceed full scale the run refuses 'ERROR: The attack may distort with this gain level.' (content-dependent - a peak-0.92 source refused gain 1.5; the same material scaled to peak 0.32 accepted it). All four parameters and the envtype flag refuse breakpoints. Deterministic; stereo accepted.
musical_use: Surgical accent placement: give a chosen syllable, note-start or grain its own sforzando without touching the rest of the file - the offline equivalent of riding a fader for one beat. Use short onset (5-20 ms) + moderate decay (50-200 ms) for a percussive spike; longer onset makes a push INTO the moment (agogic accent). Works musically as articulation repair (restore an attack softened by stretching or blurring - CDP's manual pitches exactly this), or as phrase-level punctuation applied at different times across copies of the same material. Mind the headroom gate: keep peak x gain under 1.0 - attenuate first (modify loudness) if the source runs hot. Mode 4 (max-level attack point) skips this safety check and will happily render clipped-over floats - preferred only when you want that.

time.description: Exact time of the attack point. CDP-enforced 0 to indur-0.005 (input-dependent: '(0.000000 to 1.995000)' on a 2 s file). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1'). Scalar only.

gain.description: Amplification at the attack point. CDP-enforced 1-32767 ('Parameter[2] Value (-1.000000) out of range (1.000000 to 32767.000000)') - boost only, no attenuation. Runtime content gate: refuses 'The attack may distort with this gain level.' when source peak x gain would clip. Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

onset.description: Rise time of the boost envelope into the attack point. CDP-enforced 5-32767 ms. Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

decay.description: Decay time of the boost envelope after the attack point. CDP-enforced 5 to just under the input duration in ms (input-dependent: '(5.000000 to 1995.000000)' on a 2 s file). Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

envtype.description: Boost envelope shape: 0 linear, 1 exponential (default). Hard-enforced 0-1 ('Parameter[5] Value (5.000000) out of range (0.000000 to 1.000000)') - no undocumented shapes. Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

examples.expected_use: Only the ~0.55-0.68 s region lifts; duration unchanged. Requires source peak x 1.5 < 1.0 or the run refuses.

examples.description: Push into a downbeat (slow rise, quick release).
examples.expected_use: Linear 300 ms crescendo peaking exactly at 1.0 s, back to unity 50 ms later.

known_issues: HEADROOM GATE (verbatim, exit 255): 'ERROR: The attack may distort with this gain level.' - content-dependent (source peak x gain vs full scale). Modes 1-3 all enforce it; MODE 4 DOES NOT (probed: mode 4 with gain 2.0 on a peak-0.92 source rendered a 1.833-peak float file with no complaint) - an inconsistency to remember when switching modes via execute().
gain's floor is 1.0 - this tool only boosts. To duck a moment instead, invert the logic with envel scaled or a mixfile level ride.
time/decay bounds are input-dependent (refusals quote per-file ranges).

Sibling modes 1 (gate-detected attack: extra gate param 0-1 replaces time), 2 (approx-time +-200 ms) and 4 (file max, no time param) share the remaining argv; only mode 3 is curated - its exact-time contract is the reproducible one. Others via execute().
All params scalar-only (breakpoints refused, parameters 1-5). Deterministic; duration static and exact; stereo accepted.
